title: Bash tool call reported as user-rejected still executed (git push, then git commit)
details:
- **What happened:** Two Bash tool calls returned the standard rejection result ("The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use. The tool use was rejected...") yet their commands actually ran. (1) A compound `git status --porcelain && echo ... && git push -u origin <branch>` was reported rejected; a later `git fetch` revealed the remote branch existed at the exact local HEAD, including a commit created minutes earlier. (2) A compound `git add -A && git commit -F- <<'EOF' ... EOF; git log; git push` was reported rejected; `git log` later showed the commit had landed locally (the `git push` portion had NOT run). Expected: a rejected call performs no side effects.
- **What the user said:** In case (1) the user had interrupted specifically to prevent the push: "before we do that, make sure we have the latest base develop". The push had already happened. User did not comment on case (2); observed by the model.
- **Repro:** Interrupt/reject a Bash call whose command is a compound `A && B` chain containing a side-effecting git command. Observed twice in one session; in both cases an earlier segment of the chain executed while a later one did not, suggesting the rejection lands mid-chain rather than before execution.
- **Evidence:** Session on branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart`. Case 1: remote branch appeared at commit `fd3ae184` with no local upstream recorded, and a `Deploy Preview` workflow run was triggered. Case 2: commit `517d2657` present locally, `origin` still at `43ee76b2`. Both recoverable (case 2 was amendable since unpushed), but case 1 was an outward-facing push the user had explicitly interrupted to stop.
